name: power_24vac
text: At the VAV box, measure the voltage at the actuator terminals: is it missing or outside 22 to 26 VAC?
photo_hint: Open-door view of the whole VAV box, with the round actuator motor and the small wire terminals both visible.

name: control_signal
text: With the VAV box commanded open, measure the control signal at its actuator input: is it missing (under about 2 V on a 0-10 V actuator)?

reading.quantity: DC control signal with an open command

photo_hint: The actuator motor and the controller it is wired to, close enough that you can see the wire terminals.

name: manual_damper_test
text: At the VAV box, disconnect the actuator and turn the damper shaft by hand: is the damper stuck or binding?
photo_hint: The actuator on the side of the box and the metal shaft it turns, plus the small release button or lever if you can see one.

name: damper_linkage
text: At the VAV box, inspect the damper linkage, seals and stops: is the linkage loose or slipping, or the damper not reaching fully open or fully closed?
photo_hint: The actuator, the shaft and the arm or clamp that connects them to the damper, from the side.

name: controller_leds
text: At the VAV box, look at the controller status lights and event log: is it dead, showing a fault, or off the network?
photo_hint: The small controller circuit board with its blinking lights, with the wiring and the label next to it.

name: sensing_ports
text: At the VAV box, inspect the flow-sensing ports and tubing: are ports clogged, or tubes kinked, loose or swapped (high and low)?
photo_hint: The round air-inlet of the box where the small plastic tubes and the little pressure sensor connect.

name: flow_vs_gauge
text: At the VAV box, compare the controller's pressure reading with a gauge on its flow taps: do they disagree by more than about 10%?
photo_hint: The controller and the small tubes or taps on the box inlet, and the gauge if you have one.

name: k_factor
text: Compare the K-factor programmed in the controller of the VAV box with the value on its nameplate or submittal: do they differ?
photo_hint: The label or sticker on the box (nameplate), close enough to read the numbers.

name: static_at_box
text: At the VAV box, measure the static pressure at the inlet: is it below the minimum for its size (about 0.25 to 0.5 in. w.c.)?
photo_hint: The round inlet of the box where the air comes in, with a few feet of the duct in front of it.

name: reheat_coil
text: At the VAV box, inspect the reheat coil and valve (or electric element and connections): is the valve stuck or leaking, the coil fouled, or a connection damaged?
photo_hint: The heating coil or electric heater section on the outlet side of the box, with the pipes, valve or wiring.

name: ahu_visit
text: Go to the air handler: is the supply fan stopped, tripped or in fault?
photo_hint: The front of the air handler showing its main fan section, status lights, and any display or door label.

name: ahu_gauge
text: At the air handler, read the duct static pressure gauge against its setpoint: is it low?
photo_hint: The pressure gauge or display on or near the air handler, close enough to read it.

name: ahu_economizer_test
text: At the air handler, override the outdoor-air damper open and watch it respond: is it stuck near its minimum, or slow or failing to modulate?
photo_hint: The outside-air damper section of the air handler or rooftop unit, showing the damper blades and the actuator.

name: diffuser_duct
text: Look at the diffuser in the room and the duct behind it: is the diffuser blocked or closed, or the duct crushed, disconnected or leaking?
photo_hint: The ceiling vent (diffuser) and, if reachable, the flexible duct above it.

name: thermostat
text: In the room, compare the thermostat or zone sensor with a reference thermometer and check its setpoint and mode: is it off, or the setpoint or mode wrong?
photo_hint: The wall thermostat or room sensor with its screen or dial visible.

name: flow_hood
text: Measure airflow at the diffuser in the room with a flow hood: is it well off what the VAV box should be delivering right now?
photo_hint: The ceiling vent (diffuser) you will put the flow hood on, and the space around it.
